name: performance
description: 8 scenarios x 3 context buckets (1K/8K/32K) x 10 targets = 240 measured rows in one jsonl; same target shares an identical question across buckets, only the context length differs; no scoring.

sampling.method: sha256(seed|upstream_id) ascending order + stratified largest-remainder quotas; independent of file row order

tokens_semantics: tokens = content tokens of messages[0].content + JSON-text tokens of tools (reference tokenizer, no chat template; one BOS per encode included); messages_tokens/tools_tokens are the two audited parts
bucket_basis: content tokens (messages + tools JSON text) counted by the reference tokenizer, one BOS per encode included; chat-template control tokens excluded

tokenizer.name: MiniCPM5-1B
tokenizer.tokens_semantics: tokens = content tokens of messages[0].content + JSON-text tokens of tools (reference tokenizer, no chat template; one BOS per encode included); messages_tokens/tools_tokens are the two audited parts

accept_rule: integer token counts: floor(0.95*target) <= tokens <= floor(1.05*target), where tokens = messages_tokens + tools_tokens (content tokens, no chat template)

window_requirements.note: Runtime window check is declared_tokens + max_tokens + context_safety_margin + decode_guard_reserve. A 32,768-token window can only host declared tokens <= 32526; the remaining 32K rows are reported as not-testable (summary.skipped), never truncated. Declared tokens exclude the decode guard.

sampling.pool_filter: raw context >= 120000 characters, deduplicated by sha1(context)

sampling.reference_rotation: sha256(42|target_id) % len(pool), target excluded; one pass of distinct 'metadata + prompt' units, never repeated

deviations.note: Declared tokens are content tokens of the user message plus the JSON text of tools (chat-template control tokens excluded). The model-side rendered prompt is larger: the reference tokenizer also counts one BOS per encoded text (see tokenizer-bos-included) and the runner appends a decode-guard message before chat-template overhead (see decode-guard-suffix), so actual input_context_tokens exceeds the declared bucket value.

The reference tokenizer counts with add_special_tokens=True, so every declared messages_tokens/tools_tokens includes one BOS token: +1 for the user message in all scenarios and +1 more for tools JSON in general_agent/search_agent (+2 total). The declared tokens therefore include a special control token even though tokens_semantics says content tokens without chat template; the +/-5% bucket bounds absorb the 1-2 tokens.

At run time benchmark._apply_decode_guard appends a second user message (36 tokens in the reference tokenizer) instructing the model to ignore the question above and write a >=250-word technical summary. Together with chat-template overhead (~10-30 tokens) the rendered prompt exceeds the declared content by ~46-69 tokens: the 1K bucket actually renders ~1.9%-11.6% above its declared value, 8K/32K by <2%. Generation follows the guard instruction, not the dataset question; this is a measurement-protocol deviation.
10 targets per scenario x bucket (240 measured requests total) is a load-shape profile for per-sample latency/TPS, not a leaderboard-scale evaluation: official benchmarks usually run every item.

Document scenarios use a character prefix of one LongBench v2 document per bucket (1K subset of 8K subset of 32K) with an identical question/options block; official LongBench v2 uses the full document with the official prompt template.

The document prefix is cut at a character offset, not at a structural boundary, so long_context prompts can end inside a JSON object/array/string and coding prompts can end inside an open Markdown code fence (for example 19/30 long_context rows have unbalanced braces). Structured closure of the sliced document is not guaranteed.
general_agent sends one BFCL v4 single-turn request with a target-first whole-function catalogue prefix; official BFCL scores multi-turn tool-call trajectories and exact arguments.

multilingual uses 10 different Global-MMLU questions rendered one per language (the same-language reference block is a load-shape extension), whereas the accuracy set and the official Global-MMLU protocol evaluate the same question in each language.
Performance rows carry no judge/gold contract: run mode never scores, SampleRecord.score stays null, and answer correctness is out of scope for this set.
instruction_following, math_logic and multilingual contexts are same-set reference blocks (other items rotated per target), not the official few-shot prompt templates.

Reference blocks are assembled from complete units (instruction / solved example / question) and then cut by character prefix, so the last unit can be partial: the final reference item may be half an instruction, half an example or half a question stem, and the cut may fall inside a multilingual question/option unit. The block is not repeated; only the tail unit is potentially truncated.

instruction_following renders each reference item as 'INSTRUCTION <k>: ids=<instruction_id_list JSON> kwargs=<kwargs JSON>' followed by the prompt. One pass of the 509 non-target items is ~44.1K tokens (> the 32K lower bound 31,129), so the 32K reference block is a single non-repeating pass of distinct units (reference_pool_cycles is always 1); this replaces the earlier doubled block.

32K rows declare 31,129-34,406 tokens; with max_tokens=50 + 128 safety + 64 decode-guard = 242 reserved tokens a 32,768-token model window cannot host the upper rows (not-testable, reported as skipped, never truncated).
